article.title: Effects of cognitive behavioral therapy on psychological and physical outcomes in adults with rheumatoid arthritis: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
article.authors: Zhang Y, Wu F, Huang L
article.abstract: Pain and functional limitations associated with rheumatoid arthritis (RA) can substantially impair patients' psychological and physical well-being. Cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) may alleviate psychological and physical symptoms in patients with RA by modifying maladaptive cognitions and behaviors and promoting adaptive coping with the disease. However, the effect of CBT in RA patients has not been systematically established.
